blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Microglial receptor biology in inherited white-matter disease

item.vignette: A 44-year-old woman develops progressive personality change, executive dysfunction, gait stiffness, and bradykinesia. MRI shows confluent frontoparietal white-matter lesions and thinning of the corpus callosum. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous pathogenic variant in CSF1R.
item.lead_in: Loss of signaling through this receptor most directly disrupts the homeostasis of which cell population?
item.difficulty_basis: Expert estimate only; requires linking CSF1R receptor biology to CNS microglia after recognizing an inherited leukoencephalopathy.
item.tested_construct: CSF1R signaling regulates microglial survival, proliferation, differentiation, and function

explanation.key_explanation: CSF1R is a cell-surface receptor tyrosine kinase for colony-stimulating factor 1. It regulates mononuclear phagocytes, including CNS microglia; pathogenic CSF1R variants can cause progressive leukoencephalopathy.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Microglia are CNS mononuclear phagocytes whose survival and function depend strongly on CSF1R signaling.
distractor_explanations.B: Schwann cells form peripheral myelin but are not the defining CSF1R-dependent population.
distractor_explanations.C: Purkinje neurons can be affected secondarily in many neurologic diseases but are not the primary CSF1R lineage.
distractor_explanations.D: Anterior horn neurons are the primary cells lost in spinal muscular atrophy.
distractor_explanations.E: Zona fasciculata cells respond to ACTH; they are not the defining CSF1R-dependent population.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize CSF1R as a receptor tyrosine kinase critical for microglial survival and function in CSF1R-related leukoencephalopathy.

evidence_map.claim: CSF1R regulates survival, proliferation, differentiation, and function of mononuclear phagocytes including CNS microglia.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Links the pathogenic CSF1R variant and white-matter disease to microglial dysfunction.
